explanation: Charles V sailed on Algiers in 1541 to take back a city the Ottomans had held since 1529, and the 1529 article says so in those words. “Capture of Peñón of Algiers (1529)”, at revision 1370609401, § Aftermath: “Over the following years, Barbarossa used Algiers as a major base for launching raids from the Barbary Coast. The huge Algiers expedition undertaken by Charles V in 1541 to retake Algiers ended in failure.” The second author, “Battle of Algiers (1541)” at revision 1375834500, § Background, dates the possession the expedition set out to undo to the same year: “Algiers had been under the control of the Ottoman emperor Suleiman the Magnificent since its help in 1529 by Hayreddin Barbarossa.” The type is `precondition-of` and not `caused`: what the 1529 capture supplied was the thing to be retaken, and neither article gives it as Charles’s motive — the 1541 article names that separately, as revenge for the siege of Buda, which this atlas does not hold. `probable`, on the articles alone (rule 22).
